title: Jump the Five
mechanic: A dictionary as a secret code

scenario.title: Masking phone numbers in logs
scenario.body: Scrambling every digit is a cheap way to keep phone numbers out of log files. A mask that misses digits leaks them, and the book's dictionary only knows '0' to '9'. People type numbers on Arabic, Hindi and Japanese keyboards too: ٠١٢, ०१२, ０１２. Mask those without breaking any of the author's tests.

character.name: Hopscotch
character.role: a kangaroo who hides phone numbers

tagline: Hopscotch keeps phone numbers secret by hopping every digit over the 5 on a phone keypad: 1 lands on 9, 2 on 8, and 5 and 0 swap places. Hop twice and you're back where you started.

brain_blurbs.real: Knows digits from every alphabet, like ٣ and ３.

rules.test_usage: Explains itself when you ask for help
rules.test_02: Numbers inside a sentence hop, the words stay put
rules.test_jumping_twice_gives_it_back: Hop twice and you get the real number back
rules.test_fullwidth_digits: Wide Japanese digits like ０９０ hop too (and stay wide)
rules.test_no_digit_survives: No digit is ever left where it was
rules.test_only_digits_change: Letters, emoji, ½ and ² don't hop
